outcome: Incidence of adnexal mass and ovarian cancers during pregnancy
Maternal outcomes (cesarean section, thrombosis, morbidity, mortality)
Fetal outcomes (prematurity, intrauterine growth restriction, preterm rupture of membrane, intrauterine death)
cohort: Women who delivered between 2003 and 2011 in the United States, identified from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project-Nationwide Inpatient Sample
finding: The diagnosis of ovarian mass during pregnancy is rare and associated with an extremely low malignancy rate; while malignant ovarian tumors increased the risk of cesarean section and thrombosis in mothers and prematurity in newborns, there was no significant increase in other maternal or fetal risks.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was significantly higher in women with ovarian masses, OR 5.92 (95 % CI 4.12-8.40).
